title: Why My Dog Stares at Me: Often Waiting, Plus 1 Oxytocin Study 👀 (Things Living In Your House #69)
description:
Why does my dog stare at me? The American Kennel Club (AKC) says dogs stare at us a lot: essentially, they are waiting for us to do something that affects them. Dogs learn that owners pick up the leash before a walk and watch for it, and the AKC says the same is true for mealtimes. In one 2015 study, owners were reunited with their dogs for 30 minutes. Long gazes went with a rise in oxytocin: dogs and owners who shared long gazes had the rise (in owners it was measured in urine), and in pairs that shared shorter gazes it stayed stable. The authors say this gaze and oxytocin loop may have supported the co-evolution of the human-dog bond; two other scientists called that conclusion premature. Not every stare is the same: the AKC says if a dog gives you a hard stare, with unblinking eyes and a stiff posture, back away and don't make eye contact, and never stare down a strange dog. General information, not safety training.

#dogs #dogbehavior #meatballmyths #shorts

Sources: American Kennel Club, Why Does My Dog Stare At Me? (updated Mar 27, 2026); Nagasawa et al. 2015, Science (abstract on PubMed); Fiset & Plourde 2015, Frontiers in Psychology (commentary).
